sources.source: Crime in England and Wales: year ending March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The current official bulletin reports an estimated 9.6 million CSEW headline-crime incidents and about 989,000 violence incidents in the year ending March 2026. It reports that 40.9% of people experienced or witnessed anti-social behaviour, while warning that the increase was inflated by questionnaire changes from April 2025.
sources.quality_effect: Adds the newest national crime-survey context while retaining sampling uncertainty, survey-versus-police coverage, anti-social-behaviour question-change, publication-language and non-locality guards.

sources.source: First time entrants (FTE) and Offender Histories: 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited 21 May 2026 release provides tables and pivot tools on first-time entrants and offender histories in England and Wales, including a listed 49.9 MB ZIP archive and separate accessible tables.
sources.quality_effect: Adds offender-entry and history context while requiring exact byte-size verification, sub-48-MiB packaging and a SHA-256 manifest before any repository ingestion; no external archive was downloaded or committed.

sources.source: Proven reoffending statistics: January to March 2024
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports a 28.9% proven reoffending rate for the January-to-March 2024 cohort: around 25,000 of 87,000 offenders committed a proven reoffence. The publication warns that three-month cohorts are more volatile and court-processing delays affect the measure.
sources.quality_effect: Adds repeat-offending context with cohort-entry, one-year follow-up, conviction-window, court-throughput, quarterly-volatility and prior-offence guards; it is not a current local crime rate.

sources.source: Knife and Offensive Weapon Sentencing Statistics: 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release records 21,091 knife and offensive-weapon offences dealt with by the CJS in the year ending December 2025 and an immediate-custody proportion of 31.2%. It states that recent figures are provisional and may change as cases progress.
sources.quality_effect: Adds sentencing context while separating offences, offenders and sentencing occasions and retaining provisional-data, court-backlog, offence-mix, age and legislation-version guards.

sources.verified_fact: The accredited projection places the March 2030 prison population between 98,000 and 103,600, with a central estimate of 100,600, and states that charging, court flows and recalls are important drivers.
sources.quality_effect: Adds capacity-planning context with scenario, policy, court-demand, recall, model-assumption and forecast-versus-actual guards; projections are not observed safety outcomes.

sources.source: Ethnicity and the Criminal Justice System 2024
sources.verified_fact: The accredited biennial compendium combines victimisation, police activity, defendants, offender management, offender characteristics, offence analysis and practitioner statistics across the criminal justice system.
sources.quality_effect: Adds disparity-monitoring context while retaining stage-specific denominators, age and sex interactions, unknown-ethnicity coverage, indictable-only court analysis and non-causation guards; observed differences do not establish discrimination or parcel risk.

sources.source: Perception and experience of police and criminal justice system, England and Wales: year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited CSEW release reports victim satisfaction with police handling in 51% of reported crime incidents and confidence that the CJS is effective among 48% of respondents.
sources.quality_effect: Adds service-perception context with incident-versus-person, reporting-selection, multiple-victimisation, survey uncertainty and perception-versus-performance guards.

sources.source: CSEW estimates of personal and household crime, anti-social behaviour and public perceptions by police force area: year ending December 2025
sources.verified_fact: The 23 April 2026 official data file provides police-force-area estimates and confidence intervals for local-police perceptions, police-and-council confidence, personal and household crime risk, and anti-social-behaviour experience.
sources.quality_effect: Adds subnational crosschecks while requiring confidence intervals, effective sample size, police-force geography, overlapping survey windows and no parcel-level downscaling.

sources.source: Women and the Criminal Justice System 2023
sources.verified_fact: The accredited compendium combines statistics on victims, police activity, defendants, offender management, offender characteristics, offence analysis and practitioners to compare female and male experiences in the CJS.
sources.quality_effect: Adds sex-disaggregated context while retaining source-year, offence-mix, age, pathway, denominator and non-causation guards; representation differences cannot be interpreted as unequal treatment without further analysis.
